newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK commissions study on electronic road pricing.
newsitem.headline: HK commissions study on electronic road pricing.

text.p: The Hong Kong Transport Department said on Tuesday it had commissioned HK$30.8 million feasibility study on the implementation of electronic road pricing in the territory.

The study by WSA-Hyder, a consortium of Wibur Smith Associates Ltd and Hyder Consulting Ltd, will examine the need and practicability of introducing electronic road pricing in Hong Kong and will take 27 months for completion in 1999.

It will also make recommendations on the essential components, cost effectiveness and the possible consequences of such a system, giving due consideration to issues concerning transport planning, system technology and public acceptance.
"A field trial will be conducted in early 1998 for about six months to confirm the reliability of the system," a government spokesman said.
The study was prompted by the recommendations of a working party on traffic congestion made in 1994.
"The working party considered pricing the use of roads as an efficient, equitable and flexible way of dealing with traffic congestion in the long term," the spokesman said.

"Instead of restraining the growth in the number of vehicles, road pricing helps improve efficiency of road use by charging variable fees for entry into congested areas or the use of overloaded roads at busy hours," he said.
The proposals put forward by the Working Party are generally supported by the public, the spokesman added.
